# DevTeardown

> Source-based developer-tool comparisons and a multilingual deal catalog.
> Prices and availability are dated observations, not live quotes or purchase guarantees.

## Comparisons

- [Stripe vs Lemon Squeezy / Paddle](https://devteardown.com/compare/stripe-vs-lemonsqueezy-vs-paddle/): There is no single merchant-of-record invoice.
- [Anthropic vs OpenAI](https://devteardown.com/compare/anthropic-vs-openai-api-pricing/): The named standard rows match: $2 input, $10 output and $0.10 cached input per million tokens.
- [Datadog vs Grafana Cloud](https://devteardown.com/compare/datadog-vs-grafana-cloud/): Grafana Cloud wins every version of this bill where the data is the problem, and the margin is an order of magnitude once cardinality passes the 10,000-series allowance.
- [AWS Lambda vs Cloudflare Workers](https://devteardown.com/compare/aws-lambda-vs-cloudflare-workers/): For a request that waits, Workers is two to three times cheaper and the gap grows with every millisecond you spend on a database call.
- [Resend vs SendGrid](https://devteardown.com/compare/resend-vs-sendgrid/): For a small service within 3,000 emails a month and 100 a day, Resend offers an ongoing free option.
- [Supabase vs Firebase](https://devteardown.com/compare/supabase-vs-firebase/): If your bill grows with how often people watch data rather than how much data you keep, Supabase wins: that dashboard is about $1,296/month of Firestore reads against $25 for one Pro Micro project.
- [Vercel vs Cloudflare Pages](https://devteardown.com/compare/vercel-vs-cloudflare-pages/): Teams whose transfer passes 1 TB or whose requests pass 10M a month should pick Cloudflare Pages if every asset fits 25 MiB: 3 TB means $307.20 of Vercel overage against $0.
- [Cursor vs GitHub Copilot](https://devteardown.com/compare/cursor-vs-github-copilot/): Teams content with Grok should choose Cursor, from $8 Plus; teams whose review runs through GitHub PRs should choose Copilot Pro at $10/user/month or above.
- [Notion vs Obsidian](https://devteardown.com/compare/notion-vs-obsidian/): Choose Notion Business if you need granular database permissions or private teamspaces: for 10 people, 10 × $20 × 12 = $2,400/year, including Notion Agent but not Custom Agent credits.
- [Bun vs Node.js](https://devteardown.com/compare/bun-vs-node/): Pick Node if your service needs an API Bun documents as missing — getPeerCertificate(), SNICallback, createHook with real async ids — or if a native addon in your tree has no build for NODEMODULEVERSION 147.
- [Prisma vs Drizzle](https://devteardown.com/compare/prisma-vs-drizzle/): Pick Drizzle if a generated client is the thing you refuse to add and you can pin 1.0.0-rc.5 having read its breaking notes.
- [Docker vs Podman](https://devteardown.com/compare/docker-vs-podman/): Pick Podman if your company sits under both free-use limits and you can fund the port, or if you are past them and want per-seat × headcount off the budget.
- [Clerk vs Auth0](https://devteardown.com/compare/clerk-vs-auth0/): Pick Clerk if most of your sign-ups never come back a second day, because Clerk bills only the ones who do — 50,000 MRU are included on a $25/month Pro plan.
- [PlanetScale vs Neon](https://devteardown.com/compare/planetscale-vs-neon/): Pick Neon if your databases sleep: suspended compute costs $0, and a branch per pull request costs $1.50 a month instead of a cluster.

## Catalog and methodology

- [Unified deal catalog](https://devteardown.com/deals/): English, Korean, Chinese, Japanese, Spanish and French views of the same inventory; country eligibility is separate from language.
- [Editorial and source policy](https://devteardown.com/editorial-policy/): evidence, limitations, corrections and shopping links.
- [Comparison evidence export](https://devteardown.com/llms-full.txt): article sections, source links and dated offer observations; not live prices.
- [Sitemap](https://devteardown.com/sitemap.xml)
